A 5% salt solution is the default for fermenting cucumbers. Weigh the
water; salt percentages refer to total weight. Below 3% the brine is a
hostel for whatever wants to grow; above 8% the ferment slows to nearly
nothing and only the salt-tolerant bacteria remain.

The critical part is keeping the vegetables submerged. A brine that
touches air goes fuzzy within days — the surface is where the mould
lands. Weights and whole leaves (grape, horseradish) hold things down
and give the lactobacilli a head start.

First bubbles appear between day two and day four at room temperature.
